slides.heading: Comparison Operators
slides.body: Comparison Operators is part of Boolean Logic and Comparisons. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Comparison Operators
slides.body: Comparison operators compare two values. Examples include >, <, >=, <=, ==, and !=.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: Comparisons are like checking who is taller, older, or equal in a line of students.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Boolean expressions must produce True or False. Use comparisons and logical operators carefully.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Check if score is at least 75 and print the result.

quiz.prompt_text: Which comparison operator checks if two values are equal in Python?
quiz.explanation: Correct! The == operator checks equality. A single = assigns a value, while == compares two values and returns True or False.

quiz.prompt_text: Arrange the following lines to assign age and check if it is at least 18.
quiz.explanation: The comment is first, then age is assigned, and finally the comparison is evaluated and printed. Both variables must exist before comparing.

quiz.prompt_text: Assign 80 to a variable named score and print the result of checking whether score is at least 75.

content.hint: Use score >= 75 inside a print() call.

quiz.correct_answer: Any valid Python code that satisfies the prompt.
quiz.explanation: print(score >= 75) outputs True because 80 is greater than or equal to 75. Comparison operators help programs make decisions.
